name: reflect
title: reflect (Brian Paul, 1995; Mesa demos)
fetch: mkdir -p corpus/mesademos && for f in demos/reflect.c util/readtex.c util/readtex.h util/showbuffer.c util/showbuffer.h images/tile.rgb; do curl -sfL -o corpus/mesademos/$(basename $f) https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/demos/-/raw/mesa-demos-8.0.1/src/$f; done
_doc: A textured table reflecting two spinning objects: the table drawn into the STENCIL buffer first (colour masked off, GL_REPLACE), the scene mirrored through it where the stencil is 1 (GL_EQUAL), then the table blended over it and the scene drawn normally. GLU builds its objects (gluCylinder, a cone among them), places the eye (gluLookAt) and mipmaps the SGI .rgb tile readtex.c loads (gluBuild2DMipmaps). It asks GLUT for a stencil buffer (GLUT_STENCIL), which is what gives gl.js one. readtex.c opens ../images/tile.rgb and, failing that, tile.rgb in the current directory, which is where the gate puts it.
